prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire system.

statement.case_for: Twisted bilayer graphene is the one shortlisted candidate where a single, simple and analytically transparent mechanism (interlayer tunnelling renormalising the Dirac velocity to zero at a magic angle in the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model) was written down first, in 2011, and was then confirmed in nature by a clearly separable experiment: the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity by the Jarillo-Herrero group. That is the pattern I trust, a clean model, a quantitative prediction and an experimental test, and it is traceable in the literature. The consequences are broad: a continuously tunable twist-angle knob, a whole moire materials field (other twisted and heterostructure platforms, fractional Chern insulators), and strong cross-disciplinary uptake. Eight members ranked it, five in their top three, and the laureate sets proposed in the openings are almost identical, which makes the allocation unusually uncontroversial for a three-person prize. Recognition now is timely: the phenomenology has been reproduced by many groups and the flat-band mechanism is well established even though the pairing mechanism is not.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit. Eva Y. Andrei's scanning-probe and transport work on twisted layers and flat-band localisation predates or runs parallel to the 2018 transport results, and Yuan Cao, the first author of the decisive 2018 papers, cannot be credited alongside the three-person limit, so the trio is open to the charge of rewarding the group leader and the theorists rather than the full chain of discovery. Earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues; Shallcross et al.) is also not captured. Second, as Eva Lindroth and Mark Pearce note, the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unresolved and twist-angle disorder complicates reproducibility, so one can argue the field is still forming and that waiting for a settled mechanism would be safer. Finally, from a theorist's standpoint, the continuum model is a minimal effective description, and a prize risks attributing to it the later understanding of correlations that came from many other hands.

responses.point: Eva Lindroth ranked twisted bilayer graphene only sixth because the origin of the superconductivity is not understood and sample-to-sample variability makes the interpretation not yet stable, and she puts the optical lattice clock first.
responses.response: I take the maturity worry seriously, but I would separate the discovery from the explanation. The prize rewards the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the observation of correlated and superconducting phases, both of which are reproduced by many independent groups; it need not certify the pairing mechanism, as the 1987 and 1998 prizes did not wait for complete theory. I agree that the lattice clock (B013) is an excellent candidate, which is why I keep it as my first alternative, and I find Katori and Ye an unusually clean pair. But I read the measurable payoff of the clock as an extraordinary refinement of precision and the twist angle as a new regime of matter. I also think her concern is partly answered by the fact that the mechanism of the flat band, which is what a citation would name, is the well-understood part.

responses.point: Olle Eriksson ranks B014 first for the theory-experiment loop, the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction followed by the 2018 discovery, and treats Andrei as a possible but not necessary displacement of one of the three names.
responses.response: We agree on the structure, and I share his reading of the loop, but I would press the Andrei question further than he does. Her early STM evidence of flat-band localisation is independent experimental support rather than a mere precursor, and if the committee wishes to honour the full experimental side, the choice is between Jarillo-Herrero alone for the transport discovery or a split. I would resist replacing Bistritzer, because the continuum model is a two-author paper whose mechanism is exactly what the citation names; MacDonald alone would be defensible only if the committee reads the prediction as his long programme on graphene bilayers. I disagree with Olle where he ranks B041 second: I would have it below the lattice clock because the 2016 prize already covers the topological idea and the allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and the omitted BHZ authors is much messier than the twisted bilayer case.

responses.point: Goran Johansson ranks circuit QED first as a genuinely new regime of light-matter coupling with lasting device impact, and ranks twisted bilayer graphene second, noting Andrei's claim and Cao's absence.
responses.response: I accept his analysis of B014 and agree that Cao's absence from the credited names is a real hole that the three-person cap forces on us. On B046 I respect the science, but I would be cautious about proposing it now. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, and a circuit QED prize so soon after would read to many outside the committee as the same subfield twice, while the Girvin and Devoret credit is unresolved. Twisted bilayer graphene is in a different part of condensed matter and has not been recognised, so I would put the novelty argument in favour of B014 rather than B046. If Goran can show that circuit QED is separable from the 2025 recognition in scientific content, rather than in application, I would reconsider its position in my ranking.

responses.point: Eva Olsson ranks the quantized conductance of quantum point contacts first as a clean, original and long-confirmed experiment, and regards twisted bilayer graphene second, with Andrei's early STM evidence a real allocation problem.
responses.response: Her argument on maturity is sound: the quantized conductance is fully understood and nearly four decades confirmed, so recognition would be overdue rather than premature. My reservation is the opposite one, that after so long the discovery is regarded as foundational tool rather than as new regime, and Landauer and Buttiker, who supplied the theoretical frame, are not credited, which strikes me as an attribution gap similar to the one she accepts for B014. Two simultaneous groups with a three-person split is also an awkward allocation. I would still rank it ahead of several candidates on pure scientific cleanliness, and I would not oppose it, but I do not think the age of a result should itself carry weight against a field that has already been shown to be reproducible and fast-growing.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can name a fair three-person set that accounts for Eva Y. Andrei's independent flat-band experiments and for Yuan Cao, who is outside the credited names.
Whether the superconducting pairing mechanism needs to be better understood before a prize on twisted bilayer graphene is safe.
Priority and fairness toward the earlier twisted-bilayer theory (continuum-model precursors) that preceded Bistritzer and MacDonald.
How much the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize and the 2016 topological prize should reduce the appetite for B046 and B041 respectively, which determines my fallback ordering.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I am a Gothenburg theorist in complex systems and have no collaboration with any credited person that I am aware of. I share an institutional environment with colleagues from Chalmers, and I note that Goran Johansson declared closeness to the circuit QED community, which bears on B046 and not on my preferred configuration.
